artists.biography:
The Charlatans (known in the United States as The Charlatans UK) are an English alternative rock band. The band's line-up currently comprises Tim Burgess (vocals), Mark Collins (guitar), Martin Blunt (bass), Tony Rogers (keyboards) and Jon Brookes (drums and percussion).
 
Former members of the band include guitarist Jon Day (Jonathan Baker) (1989-1991), vocalist Baz Ketley (1989) and keyboardist Rob Collins (1989-1996), who died in a car accident during recording of their fifth album.
 
In the UK, all of the band's eleven studio albums have charted in the Top 40 in the UK Albums Chart, three of them being number ones. They have also achieved seventeen Top 30 singles, and four Top 10 hits in the UK Singles Chart.

perplexity.description:
The Charlatans, released in 1995, is the fourth studio album by the British rock band The Charlatans. Musically, the album marks a pivotal shift in the band's sound, blending their earlier baggy and Madchester influences with a more refined, soul-infused rock style. The record features prominent Hammond organ, melodic guitar lines, and Tim Burgess's distinctive vocals, resulting in a warm, atmospheric sound that set it apart from their earlier, more dance-oriented work. Standout tracks like "Just When You're Thinking Things Over" and "Can't Get Out of Bed" showcase the band's growing songwriting maturity and their ability to merge introspective lyrics with catchy, radio-friendly arrangements.

In the context of The Charlatans' discography, The Charlatans is widely regarded as the album where the band truly found their own voice, moving beyond comparisons to contemporaries like The Stone Roses. It was their first release after the departure of guitarist Jon Baker and the arrival of Mark Collins, whose guitar work helped shape the album's more organic feel. The record was a commercial success, reaching number one on the UK Albums Chart and spawning three Top 40 singles. Critically, it was praised for its cohesion and emotional depth, cementing The Charlatans' place as a leading force in the Britpop era and signaling the beginning of their most consistent and celebrated period.
